title: Count by sevens
prompt:
Print every multiple of seven from 7 up to and including a limit, one per line. The starter reads the limit and holds the first multiple and the limit in callee-saved registers.

Write the loop: print, step by seven, and keep going while the counter has not passed the limit. Since `printf` is a function call, it is free to clobber the caller-saved registers; that is why the loop state lives in `x19` and `x20`.

## what is checked

- ten lines, `7` through `70`, for the limit in the stdin box
- the program exits cleanly
- a comparison drives the loop
- the same holds for other limits you do not see; a limit below 7 prints nothing
starter:
// print every multiple of seven from 7 up to a limit
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(i_r, x19)
define(limit_r, x20)

        .data
fmt_in:     .string "%lld"
fmt_out:    .string "%lld\n"

        .bss
        .balign 8
limit_m:    .skip 8

        .text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // read the limit
        ldr     x1, =limit_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =limit_m
        ldr     limit_r, [x9]               // last value that may print
        mov     i_r, 7                      // first multiple

        // TODO: loop while i_r is at most limit_r, printing i_r
        // each time and stepping it by seven. printf clobbers the
        // caller-saved registers, so keep the loop state in the
        // aliased callee-saved ones above.

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
